card.name: Linking words in neonatal sedation warnings
card.fires_on: Small linking marks ("and", a comma, an opening parenthesis) right after a list of neonatal effects such as hypotonia, respiratory depression or metabolic acidosis, just before the next symptom is named.

modes.label: And after symptom list
modes.description: The word "and" ends a list of neonatal signs, just before "feeding problems".

modes.label: Parenthesis before withdrawal signs
modes.description: An opening parenthesis follows "withdrawal symptoms" and introduces the symptom list.

modes.label: Comma in toxicity lists
modes.description: A comma sits between items in a list of toxic effects from benzyl alcohol or acidosis.
modes.example: toxicity (hypotension<<,>> metabolic acidosis), particularly in neonates

card.writes: It adds little that is clear; the promoted and suppressed tokens are mixed and unrelated to the text.
card.plain: It fires on the small joining words and punctuation inside lists of newborn side effects like sedation, low muscle tone and acidosis.
